- Fixed: starting a large download no longer drags the whole PC down. ripdl
  pre-allocated the file at full size as a regular file, so the first writes
  into it triggered NTFS zero-fill storms - multi-second disk write bursts
  (~7x the actual data) that made everything lag on machines with slower SSDs.
  Download files are now created as NTFS sparse files: only bytes actually
  downloaded take disk space, and Explorer shows the real free space right
  away instead of the file "eating" gigabytes it has not received yet.
- Bonding got smarter while a download runs, not just when it starts:
  - connections now migrate between uplinks on the fly. If Wi-Fi is
    over-served while the tether idles (or the reverse), ripdl closes one
    connection and re-dials it through the other link - without losing
    progress - until the split matches what each link actually delivers.
  - a link that came back to life (phone data restored, Wi-Fi reconnected) is
    revived immediately on the next probe instead of staying quarantined
    forever after two bad dials.
- `ripdl config` now shows the live HTTP bond state per link: measured
  per-connection capacity, dial weight, active connections and any dial
  failures - so "why is my second connection not used" is answerable at a
  glance.
- README documents the Windows policy that auto-disconnects Wi-Fi when a
  USB tether or cable appears (bonding needs both links alive), with the
  one-line registry fix.
